title: Draw a square with coordinate feedback
audience: Students with basic programming knowledge who are new to assembly
learningObjectives: Distinguish device commands from coordinate feedback
Control movement with bounded polling loops
Relate screen coordinates, headings, and an ordered pen trail
Explain instruction-clock timing, pauses, and stopping

steps.title: Read the robot clock and starting state

quiz.prompt: What advances the connected robot?

choices.text: Elapsed wall-clock seconds alone.
Completed simulated instructions while moving.
Opening its tool tab.

hints.text: Separate an execution tick from the IDE repaint timer.
A new session starts at (0, 0), heading zero, stopped, with pen up. The header requests 64 instructions per tick.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Map controls and feedback

quiz.prompt: Which action moves the robot toward a target?

choices.text: Set a heading and movement control, then observe feedback.
Store the target directly into x and y.
Change only a label in the data section.

hints.text: Compare what the program requests with what the device measures.
Heading, pen, and movement are controls; x and y are feedback.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Load the register base and side length

quiz.prompt: What is in `$s1` after the load?

choices.text: The address of side.
The right-display byte port.
The requested distance in pixels.

hints.text: Distinguish the result of `la` from the result of the following `lw`.
`$s0` is 0x00000000ffff8000 and `$s1` is sixteen for the default input. No control has changed.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Lower the pen before moving

quiz.prompt: Does lowering the pen immediately draw a line?

choices.text: Yes, it fills the whole board.
No; a line requires movement while the pen is down.
Yes, it moves to the input side length.

hints.text: Ask whether position has changed yet.
The pen is down, but position remains (0, 0) and movement is still disabled.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Choose east while stopped

quiz.prompt: Why use east for the first leg?

choices.text: It points into the board from the top-left starting point.
Ninety is the movement-enable value.
All headings move right.

hints.text: Use the screen-coordinate diagram rather than a Cartesian y-up assumption.
The robot is still at (0, 0), now facing east.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Enable movement

quiz.prompt: What determines the end of this leg?

choices.text: A fixed number of source lines.
The width of the IDE window.
The x feedback reaching the requested side.

hints.text: The desired distance is input; the clock determines how long the program must poll.
The robot begins accumulating completed instructions toward its next pixel step.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Poll x and stop the east leg

quiz.prompt: Why must `lw` remain inside the polling loop?

choices.text: The assembler refuses loads outside loops.
The register must be refreshed as the device coordinate changes.
The target length changes after every instruction.

hints.text: A CPU register holding an old coordinate does not update itself.
At `east_stopped`, position is (side, 0), movement is disabled, heading is 90, and the pen remains down.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Observe the first completed side

quiz.prompt: What must be visible at the corner checkpoint?

choices.text: Every prior animation frame.
A completed square already.
A stopped robot and the completed eastward stroke.

hints.text: Name the source boundary before comparing two snapshots.
For side sixteen, the trail is (0, 0) to (16, 0). No downward stroke exists yet.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Turn south and start the second leg

quiz.prompt: Which coordinate changes on a southward leg?

choices.text: y increases.
x decreases.
Both must change equally.

hints.text: Screen y points downward.
The next target is y = side, starting from (side, 0).

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Poll y and stop the south leg

quiz.prompt: What would happen if this loop polled x against side?

choices.text: It would measure y indirectly.
x is already equal, so it could stop before drawing the south side.
The port would rotate its meaning automatically.

hints.text: At the start of the second leg, x already has its final value.
At `south_stopped`, position is (side, side), with two completed strokes.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Turn west and start the third leg

quiz.prompt: What is the west leg's x target?

choices.text: Twice the side length.
The original side length.
Zero.

hints.text: Use an absolute coordinate target for each corner.
Movement begins from (side, side) toward (0, side).

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Poll x against zero and stop west

quiz.prompt: Why does the third side not close the square?

choices.text: The robot is still below its starting row.
The side length must always be odd.
A square needs five sides.

hints.text: Compare both coordinates with the initial position.
The position is (0, side), and three strokes form an open path.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Turn north and start the last leg

quiz.prompt: Why can north work now but not as the first outward leg?

choices.text: The meaning of north changed.
The robot is now below the top boundary.
The pen changes the coordinate axes.

hints.text: A direction and a starting position jointly determine the possible movement.
The last target is y = 0 while x remains zero.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Stop at the origin

quiz.prompt: Why explicitly stop at the boundary?

choices.text: A boundary automatically clears every control.
The board wraps around if the pen is down.
Clamping position does not disable movement.

hints.text: Separate coordinate clamping from the moving control state.
The trail is closed at (0, 0), heading zero, movement disabled, pen still down.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Raise the pen and finish

quiz.prompt: Does raising the pen erase the path?

choices.text: No; it changes whether future movement adds ink.
Yes; it clears all memory.
Only on the fourth side.

hints.text: Distinguish a control for future motion from stored drawing history.
The final state is (0, 0), heading zero, stopped, pen up, with four strokes retained.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Explain the square from its vertices

quiz.prompt: What evidence distinguishes a drawn square from no movement at all?

choices.text: Only the final origin coordinate.
The complete pen trail.
Only the exit service number.

hints.text: Both programs could finish at the origin; compare their histories.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Vary the length and device rate

quiz.prompt: Why is a fixed busy-wait count a weaker control method?

choices.text: It is independent of the device clock.
It always draws a diagonal.
Its distance depends on how many ticks the waiting instructions permit.

hints.text: Hold the instruction count fixed and change instructions per tick.
The square scales with the input, and the same requested path survives the changed rate.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Pause and rewind at a named boundary

quiz.prompt: Does waiting at a Debug pause move this robot?

choices.text: No; its execution clock is paused.
Yes, at one pixel per host second.
Only when the editor has focus.

hints.text: The clock counts simulated instructions, not screen repaints.
A pause itself adds no travel. Record the instruction boundary as well as the displayed position.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Compare a table-driven implementation

quiz.prompt: What must an equivalent solution preserve?

choices.text: Every reference scratch register.
The complete pen path and required final state.
The exact source line count.

hints.text: State equivalence in terms of observations named by the assignment.
Different source structure is acceptable when the actual four-stroke history and final controls agree.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.

steps.title: Verify the feedback argument

quiz.prompt: What would falsify the stopping argument?

choices.text: A different unused register name.
An additional source comment.
A long operation between the feedback read and movement stop.

hints.text: Account for the delay slot and the maximum gap between coordinate samples.
The checks cover actual device history, protected input and feedback words, final controls, and silent normal exit.

completion.reason: Executable author checks verify device behavior; native trainer and capture automation remain pending.
